operator_io_quirks: Table names mixed case: Allergy_Type, Has_Allergy, Student; column names mixed case (StuID, LName, Fname, city_code, AllergyType) — must double-quote and match case-insensitively.
All tables tiny (14/59/34 rows) so max_rows_per_table sampling never triggers; original_values are complete.
All columns notnull=0 (no NOT NULL constraints) and no CHECK/UNIQUE index beyond PKs; drop_unique_duplicates only matters for PKs.
PKs: Allergy_Type.Allergy (VARCHAR text PK), Student.StuID (INTEGER PK); Has_Allergy has NO PK (composite-free, no dedup).
FKs: Has_Allergy.StuID -> Student.StuID, Has_Allergy.Allergy -> Allergy_Type.Allergy; both parents exist and are unique (PK).
No self-references, no composite keys, no dangling FKs, no views/triggers/indexes in DDL.
Declared types: VARCHAR(n) -> String fuzzer (length arg n); INTEGER -> Number fuzzer (is_int, scale 0). No Date/Time/Bool/Bit/Year columns.
Storage classes match declared types everywhere (text for VARCHAR, integer for INTEGER); no contradictions.
VARCHAR(1) Sex and VARCHAR(3) city_code: String fuzzer length range [min,max+1] from elements, so fresh strings can exceed declared length (sqlite ignores).
AllergyType has only 3 distinct values (food/environmental/animal) but 14 rows in Allergy_Type — low-cardinality text column.
Student.Advisor is INTEGER with 18 distinct values (looks like an ID but is NOT declared FK) — TS will treat as plain Number.
Student.Major INTEGER 6 distinct (600,520,540,550,100) — code-like numbers, TS Number fuzzer will generate arbitrary ints.
operator_ts_expectations: String fuzzer for Allergy, AllergyType, LName, Fname, Sex, city_code: fresh random strings over a-zA-Z 0-9() with contamination, plus literal-pool values from train SQL.
Number fuzzer for StuID, Age, Major, Advisor: uniform ints in [-1,1] (scale 0) perturbed by +-1/+-2, plus pool values; will produce implausible ages/majors/IDs.
PK columns (Allergy_Type.Allergy, Student.StuID) get max_l0=inf so fresh draws never reused — many distinct PKs, good for joins.
Has_Allergy.StuID and .Allergy drawn from parent final columns with replacement -> duplicates in Has_Allergy (no PK) and possible orphan-free but skewed distribution.
Has_Allergy has no PK so sample_fresh_primary_keys is a no-op; drop_unique_duplicates no-op (no unique cols).
Table sizes: level 0 (Allergy_Type, Student) small (1+30u), Has_Allergy next level x4 capped 2500 — Has_Allergy may be much larger than parents, amplifying FK duplication.

Likely FN source: Number fuzzer generating Age/Major/Advisor values far outside plausible ranges (e.g. Age=0 or negative) makes aggregate/filter queries return implausible results that still 'execute'.

Likely FP source: String fuzzer contamination and fresh strings for Sex (VARCHAR(1)) producing multi-char values, and city_code arbitrary strings — queries filtering Sex='F' or city_code='BAL' may match nothing or wrong rows.
Low-cardinality AllergyType (3 values) with String fuzzer: fresh strings dominate, so GROUP BY AllergyType yields many spurious groups.
Advisor not declared FK: TS generates random ints unrelated to any Student.StuID, so self-join Student.Advisor=Student.StuID rarely matches — potential FN for advisor queries.
Literal pool from train SQL will supply real names (Smith, Linda), allergies (Cat, Dog), city codes (BAL, HKG) — these anchor String columns to plausible values, partially mitigating FN.
